mainEntity.name: Can I live in my house during a whole-house interior renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, most homeowners can stay in the house during some interior renovations, but comfort depends on how much of the home is affected. If the kitchen, bathrooms, or primary living areas are all under construction at once, moving out temporarily is often the less stressful option. For lighter projects, contractors can usually set up dust control, work zones, and temporary living arrangements so you can remain onsite. The decision usually comes down to safety, access to essentials, and your tolerance for disruption.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sometimes, yes—but it depends on how much of the home is being worked on. If kitchens, bathrooms, and major living areas are all down at once, many people choose to move out temporarily.
